text:
alina: heads up — after the network blip at 05:12 we started seeing nvme write latency climb on a subset of ephemeral hosts in us-central. GPU attaches are spiking failures. anyone already digging?

mike: yep saw a handful of attach errors, 502s from agent, and `iowait` on the nodes jumped. reproducible on two clusters.

jeff: can you paste the attach error?

alina: here's the agent error chunk: 
```
2026-03-21T05:13:47Z ERROR attach: attach failed: timed out waiting for device prepare
root cause: i/o timeout waiting for nvme write
```

mike: also saw kernel logs: `nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 0 timeout` and then `nvme: aborting command` repeatedly.

janine: storage-bot reported a scrub spike right before the network hiccup — scrub throughput doubled for a short window. could be interfering with janitor/cleanup? :thinking_face: 

storage-bot: scrub-runner: started scrub on pool-ephemeral-14 (hostset=us-central) at 05:11, concurrent jobs=6, avg throughput=380MB/s, io_ps=~2200.

ops-sre: are these NVMe devices showing SMART errors or wear anomalies?

mike: SMART looks fine, temp within expected. wear-level percentage unchanged. error counters incrementing on controllers though: media_errors+=12, crc_errors+3. not catastrophic but correlates with the i/o timeouts.

alina: hypothesis: network burst caused scheduling delay on mgmt plane, janitor/scrub overlapped heavy per-host cleanup, causing high io queue depth -> controller queue-starve -> timeouts during attach.

jeff: that sounds plausible. we should quickly mitigate attaching by redirecting new GPU allocs away from the hot hosts. can we taint those nodes?

janine: running query to find top-affected hosts: `kubectl -n infra get pods -o wide | grep ephemeral | awk '{print $7}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr` — will paste list in 1m.

mike: temp mitigation: enabling `nvme.core.nvme_max_io_queues=1`? unsure. might reduce concurrency to avoid controller thrash but could hurt throughput. any past docs?

ops-sre: hold on making kernel knob changes clusterwide. instead I'm cordoning the three worst hosts and draining GPU workloads off them to stop more attach failures.

alina: thanks @ops-sre. also can we throttle scrub janitor for the region? reduce concurrency from 6->2 and pause new scrub starts for 10m.

storage-bot: scrub-runner: reducing concurrency to 2 on pool-ephemeral-14. paused new scrub jobs for 10 minutes.

jeff: next action: run `nvme list` + `nvme error-log` on one affected node to check persistent controller errors. can someone ssh into gnode-uc-14a?

mike: on it, grabbing logs and will upload to the incident s3.

alina: also let's add a temporary routing rule to avoid scheduling new Dedicated->ephemeral attachments in us-central for the next hour. we can revert once scrub backlog finishes and queue depth stabilizes.

ops-sre: added policy `routing.block.ephemeral.us-central` for 1h. new allocs will use fallback pools.

janine: pasted candidate host list and counts: gnode-uc-14a(8), gnode-uc-14b(6), gnode-uc-14c(5) — those match drain targets.

mike: uploaded `nvme error-log` for gnode-uc-14a. showing repeated namespace timeouts and keep-alive retries. attaching snippet: 
```
Err cnt: 12
Status: Media Error
CMD: 0x02 (Write)
LBA: 0x1f4a7c
```

alina: ok. not a firmware-level wipe but controller is getting overloaded. post-mortem items: (1) add back-pressure between scrub janitor and attach hotpath, (2) add a short-circuit so attach will prefer fallback pools when local IO saturation detected, (3) expose nvme io_ps and queue-depth metrics to routing service.

jeff: agree. also worth a short-term rule in the autoscaler to avoid scaling onto hosts with scrub backlog > X.

ops-sre: tracking a rollback window: if after drains and throttles the error rate drops to baseline within 20m we'll mark mitigated. otherwise escalate to hardware team for deeper nvme health checks.

alina: status update in 15. thanks all. :thumbsup:
